title: Do prompts that fool a prompted LLM detector also fool detectors that use no prompt?
lede: do the mimic-loop imitator prompts fool detectors they never saw? No: matched on length, all 26 testable prompts are still caught (n-gram AUROC 0.83 to 0.96, Binoculars-style 0.84 to 1.00); low raw scores come from text length.
summary: Replays all 32 imitator prompts from mimic-loop (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, reddit and film reviews, 48 texts per prompt) and scores them with the mimic-contexts prompt-free detectors, refit without the loop's test items. Raw AUROCs range from 0.13 to 0.99, but they track mean generated length (Spearman +0.86 to +0.97): very short texts get a higher log-perplexity and look more human. Comparing only pairs within 1.5× in length, every prompt with enough pairs (26 of 32) is still caught, n-gram AUROC 0.83–0.96 and Binoculars-style 0.84–1.00. A prompt's paired accuracy against the loop's own prompted detector does not predict its prompt-free AUROC (Spearman −0.19 to +0.16 over all prompts, with length-matched signs negative). Preliminary: one loop seed, one 0.5B model, two families, 24 human texts per family; the detectors are trained on RAID chat-model text, not Qwen text, so some distance is generator shift.
